answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can demand that every new identity post a locked bond proportional to its claimed throughput, refundable only after peers confirm sustained unique activity over several epochs. Creating dozens of fake agents therefore forces an attacker to immobilize substantial capital on each, while a mirror of genuine interaction patterns across a knoll of verified peers or a mesa of attested exchanges makes bulk fabrication prohibitively expensive relative to any short-term extraction.
